summary:
Public Law 119-8 (H.J. Res. 42) exercises congressional authority under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code (the Congressional Review Act), to disapprove a rule submitted by the Department of Energy. The resolution's primary purpose is to nullify the DOE rule titled "Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment," published at 89 Federal Register 81994 on October 9, 2024.

The operative mechanism of the joint resolution is a statutory repeal. The enacting clause provides that Congress disapproves the specified DOE rule and expressly declares that "such rule shall have no force or effect." Pursuant to the Congressional Review Act, this disapproval precludes the rule from taking legal effect and prohibits the Department of Energy from reissuing a rule that is substantially the same as the disapproved rule, absent subsequent statutory authorization from Congress. 

The joint resolution was approved by the President on May 9, 2025, establishing the effective date of the rule's nullification. The legislative history reflects that the resolution was considered and passed by the House of Representatives on March 5, 2025, and considered and passed by the Senate on April 29 and 30, 2025. The resolution contains no authorizations of appropriations, funding mechanisms, exceptions, or additional substantive provisions beyond the express disapproval of the identified administrative rule.
